owner_rule: #5777/#5779: the Rust<->SENS link crosses ONLY the sterile Zig corridor.
note: Every corridor guard rule is DERIVED from a language-core axiom, not asserted ad hoc. The guard check_corridor_axiom_binding.py fails if a rule is unbound, if a cited axiom id does not exist in docs/language-core-axioms.md, or if a binding lacks a derivation.

bindings.derivation: G6: conformance is defined by observable behavior, not the host's architecture, so the corridor must be the DEFAULT transport, not an optional host-specific path. S2: a silent fallback to a Rust codec would be an unnamed failure.
G6: the Rust host must not be able to build a conforming CLI without the corridor. S2: build.rs asserts the pinned Zig and fails loudly, never silently reusing a stale transport.

G1: a value's meaning is observable behavior; the corridor carries only the implementation fact (width+payload), never a value's meaning. G5: the corridor lives above the implementation boundary and imports no semantic registry.
S2: an unpinned corridor version could drift silently; the version is a named, observable constant.

G6: conformance by observable behavior means every host crosses the SAME corridor. G7: the same expression means the same thing everywhere, so no host may invent its own op. Evidence includes at least one C host rejecting invalid T5 via sens_zig_f3c_pack(...)=-1, matching Rust encode_f3 fail-closed.
G1: the corridor exports only physical ops; it never assigns semantic identity.
G1/G5: a registry/host/semantic module crossing the corridor would leak a value's meaning into the transport.
G1/G6: a padded host struct is a host representation fact; the corridor uses caller-owned triplets so no host layout is observable.
S2: sterility is a named, declared contract, not an implied assumption.
G6/G7: every Rust<->SENS host crosses the one corridor. S2: a bypass must be a named, registered exemption, never a silent path.

G6: conformance by observable behavior means the migration must produce the SAME physical bytes as the one corridor, not a private Python codec. G7: the same expression means the same thing everywhere, so no second path may mint .sens bytes. S2: a bypass must fail named and closed -- --write without --zig-codec blocks, and the bridge rejects an unattested binary.
